The model’s strict semantic order makes its completed prefix a unique discovery sequence; predicate order matches the relation directory, and each next row follows the last row of its predicate. Rust still has to preserve both AVL indexes, callback and storage bounds, and complete-prefix refusal. The existing catalog selection laws express the denotation obligation; they do not verify this insertion path or establish that the supplied model is an answer set.

The selected discovery-order operation reuses normalized_selection_exact once its result is a permutation of the supplied identities. Rust must establish that the semantic index visits each discovery once, that the temporary mask selects exactly the supplied positions, and that filtering preserves typed order. ColumnRelations.row_mask_roundtrip uses the same membership, uniqueness and ordered-filter argument for numeric row order; it is not a verification of the AVL traversal. Dense traversal and sparse sorting therefore share the denotation obligation while retaining separate executable checks for ordering, scratch, interruption and transactional replacement.

Checked equality can reuse a canonical identity only after authenticating its scope and readable prefix. Equal IDs then use the same decoder; deciding that unequal IDs denote unequal terms additionally requires interning uniqueness. The Rust stores must establish that stronger invariant, including normalized aliases and exact hash-collision checks. These catalog laws do not prove it. Foreign scopes and sign-adjusted predicate views require typed comparison. Neither equality shortcut establishes numeric or ASP order. The callback before the identity probe and preservation of its refusal are executable obligations.

TemplateCatalog stores shared ordered terms, patterns and filters beneath separate semantic-owner policies. The retired relational Program retained rule topology and explicit domain/signature order. ObjectiveProgram still retains weight polarity, priority slots and ID-only closed conditions. Shared component storage creates no synthetic support or objective rule. The source compiler uses the same component schema for its constants, predicates, patterns and filters. Its private coordinates are valid only with the preparation that admitted them. Generated terms extend the vocabulary without changing the meaning of the static prefix; truth and support remain separate selections. This owner pairing and prefix preservation are concrete Rust obligations, not consequences of integer equality. CanonicalTemplates proves that decoding commutes with substitution of ordered argument tuples, including repeated occurrences and absent variables. Its variable-only case equals the existing BindingScopes.readAll operation. The identity type ranges over an available vocabulary: Rust must establish the scope and prefix checks that make its decoder total. Refinement of the concrete template storage and flat condition-node evaluator to these definitions and ObjectiveConditions.Query remains an implementation obligation. These laws neither prove source compilation nor infer answer-set membership from identity.

AtomAppender::insert_pattern_with borrows a checked projection of constants and assigned variables, reused for discovery lookup and row admission. The tuple is a mathematical sequence; the implementation need not materialize an ID vector. CanonicalTemplates.substitute_decodes supplies its substitution obligation; AtomKeys.key_identity and membership_identity relate the decoded tuple and signed predicate to extensional lookup. Rust must establish the scope, prefix, arity and complete-binding premises, preserve repeated arguments, and apply logical limits even on an occupied lookup. Shared immutable input borrows must keep each projected coordinate unchanged from validation through publication. Fixed preparation metadata, scratch/growth accounting and publication after all fallible checks remain executable obligations. Retaining a complete canonical row after refusal does not establish discovery or support membership.

Reusing a prepared canonical lookup additionally requires the same immutable tuple and unchanged logical row index until publication. The exclusive Rust entry enforces the writer boundary; index reservations may rehash storage but must not change logical membership. The prepared result contains no bucket address and is discarded on failure. These are implementation obligations for the existing lookup law, not a separate answer-set semantics or a new proof of the Rust implementation.

DerivedTerms gives registered input aliases and newly constructed terms one fresh identity scope. Input edges borrow exact immutable catalog prefixes; generated compounds retain local child IDs and borrowed constructor names. TermRead exposes both through the same typed term view. The input payload is not copied into the derived arena. Equal terms from different input owners, or from an alias and a construction, must receive the same registered identity.

The existing laws state the required semantic boundary. CanonicalCatalog.owner_transfer_preserves_interpretation requires decoded agreement when identities change owners; it does not infer agreement from equal integers. CanonicalTemplates.substitute_decodes preserves ordered child occurrences, including repetitions, once scope and prefix checks establish the decoder’s domain. StructuralBindings and Observations then state matching and completed-output laws over those decoded values. No new reduct is involved.

Exact alias interning, collision checks, cached expanded measures, borrowed lifetimes and preservation of a complete prefix on refusal or a caught callback panic remain Rust obligations. So does the absence of copied input payload. StorageOwners applies only after a complete, disjoint accounting of the shared inputs and the arena’s own capacities; logical occurrence charges do not measure physical sharing. The formula-DAG laws in DagSharing do not certify this typed term representation or its Rust implementation.

PartitionedScan proves that exact finite partitioning preserves an eligible-atom count and maximum index. Zero availability excludes a fitting strict-subset completion; one available atom must be false in every such completion. The maximum names that atom only under the count-one premise. The formula kernel distributes this scan over its workgroup’s 32, 64, 128 or 256 invocations and merges their summaries. Supported subgroup reductions may combine summaries first; no subgroup width is assumed and the final workgroup barrier remains. Its strided coverage, bounded u32 arithmetic, immutable scan inputs, atom correspondence and synchronization remain Rust/WGSL obligations. The laws justify domain narrowing, not answer-set acceptance.

Formula and tight shaders share partial_maximum in reduction.wgsl and its granted-subgroup specialization in reduction_subgroup.wgsl. The portable version publishes each lane’s value. The subgroup version takes each part’s maximum and elects one publisher. The zero identity covers empty contributions. PartitionedScan.maximum_append, maximum_permutation and partition_index_exact justify merging these partial maxima under exact finite partition coverage. Formula also computes its bounded additive partial before branching on the shared election, preserving the count that distinguishes atom zero from absence. Tight applies the maximum law with eligibility always true to the lane tallies of each individual phase, then sums those phase maxima. Combining tallies across phases before maximizing would change that path cost. Its alternating slots, resets and publication barriers remain in the consumer, including the verdict scan’s separate final barrier. False-root witnesses still precede unsupported-atom witnesses and use their existing minima. These laws establish the unsigned fold equations. Subgroup uniformity, election, finite machine bounds and the ordering of atomic publication and reads remain WGSL obligations. Source specialization selects all fragments before one checked setup allocation, including a subgroup-only tight source.

DependencySchedule preserves initial agreement with a reference valuation by induction over ready assignments. The evaluator reads only declared dependencies; those dependencies already agree, and the reference satisfies each local equation. Complete root coverage then preserves ordered observations. This explains both formula kernels’ shared original-truth schedule, before reduct masking or tight-support checking. Constructing its packed levels, preserving node IDs and proving concurrent writes and barriers refine the sequential schedule remain implementation obligations. A cached order alone does not authorize candidate truth reuse; tight checking separately authenticates its retained batch.

Both kernels compose the immutable header/operand reads and binary Boolean truth operation from formula_graph/truth.wgsl. The shared operation computes conjunction, disjunction and implication over the same wire tags; each consumer keeps its own original-truth traversal and publications. This factors those local equations without identifying formula propagation with tight incremental re-evaluation. Header/operand addressing and the consumer-specific fourth header word remain representation obligations, not consequences of the schedule law.

evaluate_original in that fragment also owns the common serial or level-ordered original-truth traversal. Both consumers retain their local node evaluation and publication rules; tight evaluation keeps its reuse flag, while formula evaluation requests fresh truth. Each level retains its storage/workgroup barriers, and the callers keep their distinct final publication boundaries. DependencySchedule.execution_preserves_agreement and observed_roots_equal state the local-read, readiness and coverage obligations. They do not establish WGSL uniformity, bounds or device visibility. Frozen propagation and the tight incremental update traversal remain distinct.

The general kernel starts frozen propagation with a reverse visit to those levels, then alternates reverse and forward visits. This is not an application of the evaluation theorem: the local operations are sound domain intersections, rather than assignments of original truth. Every transfer must preserve all satisfying completions, including under stale sibling reads, and original-false connectives remain disabled. Reordering such transfers retains that invariant. A dense sweep visits every gate and then checks strict subset availability; a fixed point or bounded stop remains a residual for exact completion. Packed-level coverage, collective barriers, atomic refinement and the changed work receipts remain Rust/WGSL obligations. No new shader-verification claim follows from reusing the schedule.

Soundness alone does not make two schedules agree. A sweep that changes nothing ends at the same fixed point under every schedule, and so in the same verdict class away from round and work limits, only if every transfer is also order-preserving in the domains it reads: from smaller domains it removes at least as much, so a stale sibling read can only weaken a step. The contract tests establish this for the binary gate transfer. For the native AND/OR group transfers and the threshold and extremum-cut projections it is a further Rust/WGSL obligation; the physical tests check verdict agreement across every workgroup size on fixtures that each size schedules differently, which is evidence, not proof. Answer sets do not depend on it: every outcome other than a refutation is completed exactly.

Optional changed-dependency propagation requires a separate wakeup argument. Its directory covers every operand and output domain, including atom aliases. Every gate starts eligible; an intersection marks both current and next generations, including intersections made by the strict-subset check. Active-word traversal assigns disjoint words to lanes and uses private seen masks to visit a gate at most once per sweep. Word reloads may discover new unvisited gates; wakes of already visited gates or completed words must survive in the next generation. If a sweep changes no domain, every pending transfer has observed that unchanged state; quiescence still leaves an exact residual query. These directory, atomic, coverage and generation invariants, and the extra storage and conservative work charges, remain executable obligations. This mode preserves the same sound local transfers and exact residual completion; existing Lean laws do not verify its implementation.

Optional incremental group propagation retains permission counts for native AND/OR operand occurrences. Initial counts follow frozen-domain and root setup at a uniform barrier. Each uniquely removed physical-domain bit decrements all of its operand incidences before publishing wakes; the gate’s separate output dependency does not decrement those counts. Delayed notifications leave counts as overapproximations, so they can postpone deductions but must preserve every compatible completion. Distinct physical slots still determine unique witnesses, even when one atom occupies several operand positions. Initialization, occurrence multiplicity, atomic no-underflow, notification ordering, candidate isolation and admitted storage/work remain implementation obligations; FormulaChains does not by itself verify this concurrent representation.

The closure route’s CPU oracle charged a payload amount before each comparison or copy through Work::charge; it was removed with that route, and WorkCharge remains as a statement. It equates an available work prefix with repeated unit charging under unchanged control, including exact quota exhaustion. Formula source admission instead checks an entire proposed charge before changing its counter.

The pure zetesis_algebra::Meter::check_wide_receipt checks a whole request with checked u128 addition and an inclusive ceiling. It returns a proposed total without changing a receipt or establishing that the work ran. Meter::check_receipt widens its u64 receipt and ceiling into that same calculation; Meter::charge_receipt delegates to the narrow check, then commits a successful total into the caller’s sole accepted counter. The observation evaluator keeps its explicit cancellation/deadline poll before this operation and preserves its source site and complete Statistics on failure. Importing evaluation work for later rendering does not reconstruct a meter or reject a lower limit early; the next charge, including zero, checks that limit. AtomicWork characterizes complete-demand admission, additive success and unchanged refusal. above_new_limit_refused and charge_zero cover imported receipts and checked zero requests. accepted_composition equates two successful receipts under one ceiling with their combined request; it does not equate refused traces or permit combining the caller’s control observations.

Formula source check_work classifies admission before its control observation: refused requests observe control before returning their native failure, while admitted requests use the existing cadence. count_work records actual work in Pending before updating the local count; checking a maximum does not count it. A smaller actual charge requires an unchanged prefix and ceiling and an actual amount within that maximum. Counters::absorb instead checks admission, counts completed work, then observes control: interruption cannot erase that work, and admission refusal performs no internal poll. Source overflow preserves its saturated attempted-demand diagnostic. AtomicWork.accepts_iff_fits describes the scalar preflight, not these caller invariants, native errors, control traces or Pending settlement.

Source term expansion retains its u128 accepted-work field and leading site-bearing control poll, including for zero requests. It uses check_wide_receipt; on supported 32/64-bit hosts, its usize ceiling is below u128::MAX, so mapping overflow to the native saturated attempted-demand diagnostic preserves refusal. TermWork does not publish through Pending.work. A tentative budget clone copies enforcement history but forks an empty pending account; only its newly accepted ScalarBytes charges enter Pending, before their local count is committed. Return, unwind and drop settlement publish the pending charges. These control and publication steps remain Rust correspondence obligations.

Search budgets reuse the same pure check for local work admission and the committing operation for a bulk receipt after its quota succeeds. Their explicit control poll and work-before-decision order remain unchanged. The local quota retains its existing saturating admission at the largest u64 ceiling; a carry then reports CounterOverflow at receipt publication. Shared leases can instead consume part of a request before refusing, leaving the unsuccessful local bulk receipt unchanged while retaining that work in the joined account. These native error and permit protocols are separate from AtomicWork’s scalar laws.

Shared direct charges check the real committed count against that count plus currently available permits. This accepts exactly the requests covered by available permits; outstanding grants remain unavailable. The conserved total is the greater of the initial limit and imported work, so this derived ceiling fits u64 even when the imported prefix exceeds the authored limit. Refusal retains all fields; success subtracts available permits before publishing the new committed count. The scalar law does not prove mutex behavior, concurrent settlement or progress of waiting workers.

Domain analysis and answer projection use the same borrowed operation. zetesis_domain::numeric::Budget::work keeps its existing Cell<Statistics> mutation boundary; KeyWork::step retains its own accepted-step receipt. Neither adds a control poll. Terminal-definition classification’s Engine::work uses the same domain helper for its single-unit requests, preserving typed stops and withholding partial certificates. These requests fit u128, and a refused charge reports the exact wide Stop for work. The projection Work in zetesis-solve retains its explicit poll before admission and preserves its native u64 overflow priority: a refused demand above u64::MAX maps to ProjectionError::Overflow, while other refusals retain the exact work-limit payload. Every u64 carry exceeds every u64 ceiling, so this mapping occurs before any receipt can change. Each caller retains one work counter and its other statistics; no stored meter or duplicate account is introduced. AtomicWork describes their representable-sum admission and unchanged refusal, not these native error mappings or control observations.

GPU relation planning also uses charge_receipt for its full-scan estimate. Each query retains its validation before its representable u64 accumulation; the authored whole-plan ceiling is checked only after all query costs. This estimate is neither scheduled nor completed device work. Those receipts are still published at submission and validated completion respectively. The scalar laws do not establish query costs, transport correctness or device execution.

These are natural-number scalar laws. They do not verify the public MeterWorkError::Overflow branch, u64/u128 conversions, exact error payloads, polling or Rust execution. The observation adapter’s invariant assertion relies on its inspected count producers making a representable u128 sum; hypothetical overflowing private calls are outside that correspondence. The existing prefix-consuming WorkCharge laws remain unchanged and do not establish atomic refusal. The reading guide separates those policies and the remaining implementation obligations.

The byte dimension’s zetesis_algebra::MeterBytes::observe_peak, observe_peak_usize and observe_peak_u64 share one scalar calculation at u128, usize and u64 widths. Each borrows the caller’s actual peak, publishes max(previous, total), then checks only the supplied total against its inclusive ceiling. Diagnostic widening preserves the native values; no converted peak or current/live account is introduced. The stateful observe assigns current before delegation; arithmetic preparation retains its leading poll and records requested envelopes, while frozen-positive witness completion retains its requested preflight, allocation, actual-capacity observation and charged-copy order. Refusal retains the selected observation in peak; a historical peak above a new ceiling does not itself refuse a fitting total. These are distinct caller policies around one shared maximum/check. Catalog replacement observation retains checked overlap construction, then peak publication, retained-size arithmetic and commit, then any overlap refusal. Retained-size overflow still takes precedence over that refusal. Answer projection likewise keeps its retained-capacity write before constructing the live total; an unrepresentable total leaves peak unchanged. Its constructor observes actual capacity only after the existing preflight and allocation. Neither consumer treats refused proposals as observed allocation or adds a control poll.

Table and relation capacity observers retain their usize peak fields. Table requested admission raises peak only on success; relation requested preflight does not raise it. Both retain actual observations before byte-ceiling refusal. Table checks actual usize arithmetic and observes peak before committing live. Relation reserve converts and commits actual live before observing peak; replacement commits retained live before converting the overlap. A refused overlap conversion therefore preserves that live commit and the old peak, whereas an actual byte-ceiling refusal retains both updated fields. Requested checks, allocation, copy-work charges and release order remain distinct from this shared scalar observation.

Observation wildcard-key replacement retains requested preflight, charged allocation preparation and actual-capacity refusal before replacing its old buffer. Compiled metadata likewise records its actual peak before refusal; component errors propagate before the enclosing capacity refusal. These callers borrow their existing u128 peak. Source attribution, nested-owner receipts and the distinction between requested and actual storage remain unchanged.

Generator dependency preparation also borrows its existing u128 peak. It records requested envelopes and actual capacity before refusal, but commits its current byte count only after admission succeeds. Reservation keeps its leading control poll and existing requested-before-allocation order; the shared observation adds no work charge or poll and does not change the selected dependency preference.

MeterBytes::check exposes the same pure inclusive-ceiling calculation without recording a peak. Native aggregate admission uses it for requested storage and logical byte envelopes, while its actual-capacity observations borrow the existing u64 peak. Current-capacity conversion and publication still precede peak conversion; an unrepresentable peak fails before the storage ceiling is checked. Logical peak assignment remains distinct from an observed maximum. Source support publishes its existing byte event before checking the ceiling; shared storage leases retain their atomic replacement and release ownership. These adapters add no polling, allocation or second byte account. The same pure check serves catalog requests, evaluation workspace admission, tight-plan logical bytes, partition construction, projection capacity and count-plan payloads. Each caller retains its preceding checked arithmetic and native width conversion. Partition dimensions are recorded before refusal; count-plan payloads commit only after admission. Domain inspection also uses this decision, on cumulative inspected text rather than retained storage, with its original Cell receipt and success-only publication.

BytePeak proves the two decisions, retained maximum, coverage, zero behavior and independence from the historical peak. successive_receipts composes only the retained maxima; it neither equates decisions nor permits continuing after a refusal. The reading guide separates these scalar laws from actual capacity, allocation/release ownership, finite-width total construction, typed failures, polling and Rust correctness.

The closure route’s PreparedQueries, one exact-program preparation that candidates reused with private truth state, was removed with that route. The reuse argument stated for it remains as text and has no Rust counterpart now. In that implementation, changed preparation owners retired retained workspaces, even for the same program. Those admission and lifetime checks were separate implementation obligations; the closure laws did not prove them. Historical regressions checked identity sharing, preserved refusals and retained-answer isolation.

The removed closure batch oracle partitioned ordered candidate occurrences into disjoint ranges, each with an exclusive workspace. The following shared accounting law remains general; the prepared-query accounting describes that historical batch consumer. Its coverage obligation is that splitting preserves every occurrence once and ordered concatenation restores the input sequence. Its storage obligation includes shared preparation, idle capacities and active reservations without counting shared headers twice. StorageOwners.shared_idle_active_within_limit sums explicit shared and idle bounds with an active bound of max(retained, allowance) per owner. The batch maps allowance to the scalar limit minus the prepared queries’ retained bytes and its shared closed fact rows/index subtotal, after checked subtraction. That fact subtotal is counted once in the shared component; each workspace still admits its full fact base independently. Vocabulary retains its existing per-workspace accounting. The separately allocated query-owner header enters the shared component once; its remaining immutable payload has a separate preparation ceiling. An empty batch reserves only retained storage. The consumer must account for every named region with disjoint owner entries and count the shared component once. The pointwise capacity bounds, Rust measurement, cache retirement, checked arithmetic and range scheduling remain implementation obligations. The theorem does not establish a hard allocator or RSS cap, including on a refused allocation. Reused capacity can increase retained space or change work counts; neither this law nor semantic equivalence proves a speedup.

The removed independent scalar rounds used the same occurrence partition over stable catalog insertion IDs. The DeltaRounds premises remain general. DeltaRounds.coverage_of_first_delta requires a correspondence between those IDs and complete body bindings. delta_step_exact then preserves the complete inflationary step when old consequences are already present; latched_constraints_exact additionally requires exact prior constraint history. Bootstrap handles zero-positive rules and constraints. In the retired relational representation, explicit core fact tables represented the same zero-positive headed occurrences: Program::rules() had to preserve their signed atoms, duplicate occurrences and anchors, and FactRef::as_template() had to denote that head with empty bodies and filters. The old oracle emitted these heads through the same binding and record_head path; its incremental indexes contained only templates, since a fact reads no predicate. delta_step_exact therefore uses the same old-consequence premise after bootstrap. The shared closed store supplies identity only; each workspace starts with empty discovery and truth. The historical full/delta, dense/tree, source-order and reuse tests exercised these obligations, but did not prove the Rust interning, occurrence mapping, allocation ledger or lifetime implementation.

These premises explain why the final no-change round can combine its selected scans with completed history instead of revisiting every old binding. They do not certify the Rust matcher, cache boundaries, failure cleanup or shared-world/device schedules. The delta-round guide records the historical owner and publication boundary for those premises.

Eager support joins partition new tuple combinations by their first new source occurrence. DeltaJoins.partition_complete proves coverage and partition_disjoint proves uniqueness. Source occurrence identity survives execution-order changes and repeated predicates. The Rust certificate must select only the eligible positive producer grammar; posting slices must denote the specified old/new intervals. Rich producers and final authored-body validation retain separate complete scans. These laws establish the partition, not the source evaluator or termination of value generation.

The join planner receives the partition before choosing its execution order. It need not first prepare an unrestricted order. Relation handles belong to the join’s immutable support snapshot; a prepared rule cannot retain a directory position across support publication. These choices preserve the same occurrence partition. Handle resolution, comparison readiness and admitted work remain Rust obligations.

The optional multiples selector composes this partition with necessary row selection. Its scalar totality proof covers the full immutable support snapshot; it does not establish completed-family evidence. Matching value postings are intersected with the interval of the original occurrence before they are offered to the cursor. This retains every contributing binding within that partition, the premise of DomainBindings.guarded_continuations_exact.

BoundedMultiples.bounded_multiple_iff supplies the scalar arithmetic identity: for a positive divisor d, the values in lower..upper with zero truncating remainder are exactly d*k for integer factors between (lower + d - 1) / d and upper / d, using floor division. multiple_membership composes this identity with finite interval enumeration; divisor one and empty intervals need no special premise. The implementation must establish the selector’s domain and source totality, finite-width arithmetic, exact posting and interval intersection, row ordering, snapshot lifetime and charged preparation. Neither the arithmetic nor partition laws verify those Rust operations or allow generic computed-table selection during a support round.

Meter::check_count shares the checked-addition and inclusive-ceiling body with wide work admission, while keeping named resource counts at their native usize width. Positive and stratified dependency counters retain native Overflow; source-program counts retain their saturated diagnostic on overflow, including when the authored limit is usize::MAX. Original counters publish only successful results, and no poll is added. AtomicWork supplies the whole-request admission laws under the count’s natural-number interpretation; AxisFolds.BoundedSum characterizes native-width overflow separately from the configured ceiling. These scalar laws do not identify counted source events with solver work or verify the adapters’ diagnostic and mutation order. Objective construction also uses this count admission for proposed formula nodes and operand occurrences. Its work tick still precedes node admission, which precedes operand admission; subsequent validation and the sole graph transaction retain their existing order and failures. Projection keys and retained world-view counts use the same operation. Key lookup still precedes new-key admission; answer-count refusal precedes atom-count refusal, which precedes retained-payload admission and allocation. Formula transactions compute all checked dimensions before applying their original ordered ceilings; whole-theory admission still recounts actual occurrences. These decisions neither change the graph’s shape requirements nor authorize a cached-count shortcut.

Meter::check_wide_count shares that calculation at u128 width. Source expansion uses it for templates, values, origins and cumulative scalar-byte charges, preserving the resource names and existing counters. These byte charges are not actual storage or peak observations. Representable excesses retain the full demand; overflow maps to the existing saturated source-limit diagnostic. That mapping relies on supported 32/64-bit hosts having usize ceilings below u128::MAX. Polling still precedes admission; successful scalar-byte charges publish to their existing pending receipt before the local counter commits. Domain count checks use this pure operation on already-computed demands, with zero additional demand and the original named refusal. Output conversion uses the corresponding wide work check after polling and publishing each attempted symbol step. A refusal retains that attempt; cancellation before the increment does not add one. The inherited increment’s finite-width behavior is unchanged; the scalar admission laws do not prove that this earlier increment cannot overflow.

Tight GPU planning uses the same pure work check for optional schedule and retained-truth increments, bounded by both the authored allowance and the u32 wire representation. The returned total is a proposed device allowance, not executed work; route selection and physical execution remain separate contracts.

Parallel exact queries lease bounded work allowances from one shared owner. WorkPermits partitions the allowance into spent, available and outstanding permits. Granting preserves that total; settlement records consumed work and returns the unused part. Empty availability is not exhaustion while a grant remains outstanding. After a grant is fully consumed, Rust commits its used permits and attempts to acquire a replacement under one ledger lock. Successful renewal composes settle_conserves, with consumed and granted amounts equal, then grant_conserves for a replacement bounded by availability. A successful renewal returns no unused permits and retains an outstanding replacement, so it cannot enable a previously blocked waiter. Settling the last outstanding grant with no available permits must wake waiters even though no permits were returned. The Rust implementation must additionally preserve conservation and these notification obligations under word arithmetic, locking, unwinding and cancellation; the Lean laws do not prove condition-variable progress. A joined batch records spent operations only after all leases settle; a lease is not evidence of candidate execution or membership.

zetesis_algebra::PermitLease supplies the incremental window used by the stable search lease. It and Meter share the consume-one, bounded-prefix and detach-before-publication operations over borrowed views of their actual fields. WorkPermits.take_preserves_window and take_partitions_remaining justify bounded consumption; refund_preserves_window and settlement_partitions_grant describe returned permits and the exact transfer receipt. The local lease clears its grant; the cumulative meter retains its charged history. These are different post-settlement states governed by the same used/unused partition, not interchangeable admission policies.

For runtime::copy_words, let c be charged work, L the admitted cumulative limit, with c <= L <= u64::MAX, and n a nonempty copy run covered by n <= L - c. The covered-success case of WorkCharge.repeated_eq_charge identifies n unit charges with one charge of n, both ending at c + n. Instantiating the numeric WorkPermits.Window with granted = L and remaining = L - c, take_partitions_remaining and take_preserves_window give the same remainder and used count. This cumulative view is not the source account’s outstanding grant; settlement uses that owner’s actual window and settlement_partitions_grant. At an empty balance the copy retains the original one-word charge and write, so refill, polling, refund and refusal boundaries remain unchanged. No exhausted-batch law justifies charging across that boundary.

The Rust argument additionally requires representable counts and slice bounds, one original mutable-backing acquisition, and an infallible u64 copy with no allocation, user callback or intermediate control observation. These premises make the intermediate reordering unobservable at the existing operation boundaries; they do not justify batching fallible maps or larger atomic primitives. Exact quota and stopped-prefix tests are regression evidence, not a Lean proof of Rust’s finite arithmetic, borrowing or callback behavior.

Renewal remains inside the source’s existing lock, with control observed before locking. Its callback must operate only on that source account, without re-entering the same lease, and successful refill leaves a positive unconsumed grant. Ordinary settlement still detaches before acquiring the source lock. The stable wrapper retains drop settlement; the common window owns neither a source nor a destructor refund. Its scalar laws do not authenticate callback discipline, finite-width arithmetic, cancellation, locking or unwinding. Whole-request admission retains refundable partial top-ups; incremental takes retain consumed prefixes when a later refill fails. Their zero-request and polling rules remain distinct and are checked at the concrete Rust boundaries.

Quota::replenish makes a bounded operation’s unused borrow explicit when it needs more permits. Its default preserves cumulative partial grants. A shared lease instead returns that borrow to its original window before settling and waiting for a replacement that covers the next atomic minimum. The meter writes back the returned ownership on success and refusal alike; its performed-work count does not change during replenishment. WorkPermits.refund_then_settle establishes conservation and the exact committed prefix under the owned-borrow premise. settled_replacement shows that a new grant adds no performed work; unused_window_does_not_commit covers a wholly unperformed borrow.

The new grant is requested only after the old window is settled, so a waiting worker retains no unused permits needed by a peer. If the available allowance cannot cover the atomic minimum and no grants remain outstanding, the operation is refused without running. Some allowance can remain unused. These laws do not prove the minimum-aware admission, notification, polling or unwind behavior; the concrete adapter must preserve those contracts and report no completion for a refused operation.

Whole-kernel attempts use Meter::under_reservation with an already admitted Reservation. The common operation validates that returned work does not exceed the grant before committing it. This supplies the consumed-within-grant premise of WorkPermits.settle_conserves; a native failed result with a valid receipt settles that receipt in the same way as success. Without a usable receipt, the shared guard retains its existing conservative settlement of the full grant. The caller retains its zero-allowance policy and cumulative receipt publication; acquiring, waiting for and dropping a shared grant remain Rust obligations. These laws do not verify the callback, the guard’s destructor or the concrete transaction implementation.

The parallel region walk keeps one lease per worker across its consecutive regions and settles it before stealing or waiting for another region and before sending a model; a reservation settles it first, and exit or unwinding drops it. The ledger is therefore locked about twice per grant rather than twice per region, while no unused permit is held where the worker could block. At the single-read boundary, exhaustion is reported only when no permit is available or outstanding. Atomic operations additionally need their complete minimum as described above. The total work bound is unchanged, but near a small allowance a peer can wait until a busy worker’s local run ends before permits return, and mid-run statistics trail committed work by up to one grant per worker. Its shared allowance includes coordinator certificate preparation; each worker reserves a finite checking bound before running its certificate and settles its actual returned work. The bounds follow the checkers’ charged visits: nodes, operand occurrences, roots, producers and atoms for tight checking; atoms, nodes, operand occurrences and roots for positive or stratified checking. An unwind consumes its reservation conservatively and yields an incomplete worker failure. Returning unused grants before an idle wait, releasing blocked sends before joining on iterator drop, and counting joined certificate checks are Rust lifecycle and accounting obligations, beyond permit conservation. The bounded subprocess regressions in zetesis-stable/tests/integration/parallel_regions.rs exercise shutdown and idle grants; the certificate regressions compare scalar and parallel region and construction work, check that every certified check completes within its reservation, and reject an insufficient shared allowance. An injected worker unwind also checks that idle peers wake and coverage remains incomplete.

The native parallel walk keeps one deque per worker. Its owner removes the newest region, and an idle worker tries to steal the oldest region from a peer. Each deque has its own mutex; a thief skips a busy deque. Payload preparation, narrowing and membership checks hold no queue lock. A split first reserves entry capacity for both children fallibly, then raises the unresolved-region count by one before publishing either child under the same queue guard. A resolved region decrements the count once. Taking or stealing only transfers ownership. Thus pending and active regions remain one frontier until refuted, split or checked, and an idle worker can establish termination only when the count reaches zero. Idle workers wait at a gate: the resolution that reaches zero, a stop and a close each wake them after changing the count or the closed flag. A waiter registers in an idle count under the gate, issues a sequentially consistent fence and then re-checks both conditions and the peers’ queues before waiting, so none waits past the end of the walk. A split publishes its children, releases its queue, issues a sequentially consistent fence and then reads the idle count without the gate, taking the gate to wake one waiter only when one is counted. The two fences are totally ordered, so either the waiter’s re-check finds the published child or the publication counts the waiter, whose gate it then waits for until the waiter is waiting. The wait stays bounded, which is how an idle worker sees a cancellation, or a region left in a queue its re-check found busy; completeness never depends on a wake. The memory-ordering argument is a Rust obligation, exercised by a lost-wakeup protocol harness. It rests on a premise about the platform’s mutex: releasing it and try_lock are atomic operations on its lock word, which the fences order.

Before its workers start, the walk runs on the calling thread: the coordinator takes the newest region of deque 0 as a worker takes its own, and decides it with the same per-region step. At engagement every outstanding region is in deque 0 and none is in hand, except at most one leaf held by its published query, whose pending regions are all in the published-region deque 0, so the workers start with the count equal to the regions in the deques plus that leaf. The coordinator publishes only once its engagement deadline has passed, and the pull then engages at once, so no query is running on the workspaces engagement releases. The coordinator phase and this handoff are Rust refinement obligations beside the queue and gate protocols.

A candidate’s subset query may be published for any worker to serve. The traversal surrenders its pending regions, the one it was about to narrow included, so those and the regions it visited partition the query’s root, and each published region is one pending node of the query’s coverage tree. InnerQuery.exhausted_walk_stable, emitted_refutes and exhausted_walk_decides compose Pending.Walk.exhausted with ReductRegions.stable_iff_no_countermodel: a walk of the query tree that empties its frontier without emitting a leaf proves stability, any emitted leaf refutes it, and an emptied walk’s verdict is whether it emitted one, whoever held each region. The Rust obligations are the query cell’s: its count of live regions is set to the published regions’ number before any is visible, raised by one before a split’s children are visible, and lowered once per region refuted, reaching the candidate itself, yielding a validated countermodel, or dropped after the query is decided, so it reaches zero only when the query’s frontier is empty; a server writes its witness or stop before its release decrement, and the decrement that reaches zero is an acquire-release read-modify-write, so the stable verdict sees every earlier one; one compare-and-swap decides the resolver; a validator’s refusal or stop sets the cell’s stop before its region is retired and is never counted as a resolved region; the published leaf counts in the walk until the cell is decided, so the walk’s count cannot reach zero beside a live query; and the published-region deques hold one query’s regions per worker at a time, at most its candidate’s atoms plus one, beside the candidate deque’s atom_count + 1. Unit tests drive one schedule by hand through each verdict and stop, and catch a gain counted after its children are visible, a published leaf resolved at publication, and a refused validation counted as resolved.

Pending.Step.perm and Pending.Walk.exhausted describe the abstract preservation and exhaustion laws; the atomic count, the queue and gate protocols (including the gate’s idle count) and absence of lost ownership remain Rust refinement obligations. Depth-first local order retains at most one older sibling per ancestor plus the newest children. Each split decides another atom, and stealing starts only with an empty local deque, giving at most atom_count + 1 live entries per deque. Entry capacity grows fallibly as needed and is released after joining, including a partially launched worker set. This reservation does not make region/knowledge payload cloning fallible. The owned publication boundary distinguishes a semantic split from a refused attempt to publish it. Frontier::publish_split_with reserves before consuming the narrowed parent; refusal returns that parent and the original typed error. requeue also returns its owner on refusal. Queues together with in-hand or returned parents therefore remain the pending partition at this boundary. Region.split_partition and split_disjoint justify a successful split, including a slate with one queued child and the other in hand. The refused boundary makes no further coverage-tree step: it corresponds to the identity case Pending.Walk.done, after any already completed sound narrowing. Rust must still establish exact ownership, fresh-atom selection, queue order, counter updates, capacity admission and receipt preservation; the abstract laws do not verify them.

After a typed terminal stop is committed, a non-resumable concurrent schedule may explicitly abandon the returned owner and its remaining queues. This cleanup is not a Pending.Step.refuted, and an empty container after cleanup does not meet Pending.Walk.exhausted’s premise of a covered walk to an empty frontier. Served queries must record their stop before abandonment/retirement, so neither query count teardown nor a released queue supplies InnerQuery.exhausted_walk_stable. The scalar walk’s retry and surrender contract instead retains the parent after returning a capacity refusal. These lifetime distinctions are executable correspondence obligations, not additional semantic outcomes or recovery APIs.

A native worker may retain one refuted region’s knowledge allocation for its next split. Knowledge::clone_from and CandidateKnowledge::clone_from must overwrite every logical field from the parent, preserving the same knowledge as a fresh clone and independent child ownership. Compatible arrays reuse storage; incompatible shapes are replaced. The retained bundle is not a pending region and carries no authority to narrow a different region. Complete overwrite, allocation independence and the one-bundle retention bound are Rust obligations; the frontier laws alone do not establish them. An idle worker that observes cancellation or a deadline records the typed stop before publishing closure. The coordinator may already be waiting after its own control poll; channel disconnection must retain that stop instead of establishing exhausted coverage. A concurrent close may follow a worker’s eligibility check; that already-active operation retains the existing bounded-stop contract. The Lean laws do not prove the scheduler’s progress or Rust memory ordering.

Original and frozen Narrower operations expose metered entry points returning an independent NarrowingAttempt<Failure<Q::Error>> receipt. The common zetesis_algebra::Meter reserves permits from the injected search budget through a typed Quota, at most NARROWING_BATCH (256) at a time, and spends one before each charged read, so the shared ceiling bounds execution itself. Cancellation and deadlines are polled at each reservation, so at most NARROWING_BATCH charged reads apart. A budget grants what remains when fewer permits than requested do, so a refused reservation prevents the same read per-read charging would; all earlier reads remain in the attempt and joined region counters even on a stop. Unspent permits are refunded when narrowing returns, so the receipt and the shared ledger count exactly the reads made. The failure carrier preserves the caller’s original payload; local stops retain their narrower-specific mapping. The stable adapter has no saved last-error slot. The local RegionLimits APIs wrap the same closure and meter, with their existing polling boundaries. Preservation of semantic narrowing still depends on FormulaBounds and FerrarisMask; permit conservation does not prove the reading rules or knowledge ownership. Prefix tests for original and frozen narrowing and a shared one-permit regression exercise the Rust admission/receipt boundary.

Candidate composition uses the private zetesis_stable::subject::Subject<C> interface and joint driver. Its eager adapters call Narrower::propagate_known_reserved to close the original theory, then each permanent restriction and the active bound. Each eager subject drains its propagation and support queues before reporting its local result. A streamed subject may instead decide one fresh atom and immediately return to eager closure. Only a complete late pass without changes establishes joint agreement. If no later subject changes the region, all preceding closures remain valid: their only shared mutable input is the region’s decisions. A later restriction or source consequence that decides an atom restarts from the original theory. This stopping condition depends on complete per-subject closure, exact changed flags and independent knowledge; those remain Rust correspondence obligations. The semantic preservation laws do not establish this concrete loop’s fixed point or its work and interruption prefixes.

The shared SubjectAttempt publishes each attempt’s search counts before inspecting its result, including on a failed attempt. A streamed update checks the cumulative receipt before polling, spending its existing one-unit propagation charge and mutating the mask. It spends no split decision. Source work, diagnostics and the retained source checker remain separately owned. The frozen adapter performs its existing single narrowing/selection attempt and publishes preference only after accounting; it has no candidate components. These concrete sequencing and ownership claims require Rust validation, not just the abstract Subject laws.

At that joint fixed point, the Knowledge preference operations select once, ranking the original theory’s atomic choice heads first and then the unknown-parent counts of the last subject: the active bound, latest permanent restriction, or original theory, in that precedence. With a restriction, the original theory’s unknown-parent count breaks ties through preferred_atom_with_secondary_reserved; otherwise preferred_atom_reserved retains the original-only ranking. The two knowledge values must share atom identities and be closed for the same region. The ranking charges each inspected count, one per open atom without a restriction and two with one. It reads the choice mark in the primary charge, retains its charged prefix on refusal and installs no partial preference. Packed enumeration must exclude padding and preserve ascending ties. Selecting an open atom retains the split-partition obligation of Search.CoverageTree; the existing laws do not verify these Rust ordering and accounting operations.

An implication’s child event carries truth already installed in its knowledge. A false antecedent or true consequent marks the parent true. Otherwise the revisit reads the other operand, then the parent, to apply the remaining upward and downward rules. Upward learning precedes downward teaching, and a newly learned parent retains its own queued event. The parent’s own event keeps the ordinary downward operation; chains keep their indexed operation.

These cases use the existing implication constructors of FormulaBounds.Known. Rust must establish that the event names an actual operand whose truth bit is still present, and that the parent is unmasked in a frozen-reduct query. Complete incidences, coalesced aliases, contradiction handling, event order and charged prefixes remain Rust obligations. Finite-state regressions cover distinct and aliased operands, either queued operand when both are known, and frozen child and parent boundaries. They do not formally verify the concrete queue.

The solver’s algebra

The session’s zetesis_solve::Original retains the immutable input identity against which its results were established; their original fields and accessors retain that association. zetesis_themelios::ProgramOriginal identifies retained program, part or statement evidence. Neither is the algebraic Subject C below. Renaming these owner APIs supplies no additional membership, coverage or refinement theorem.

Algebra names the objects that candidate generation and the membership check share and states the laws required of their mathematical instances. The tables give concrete Rust declaration identities and Lean identities with their kinds. Some declarations are private implementation boundaries: public callers use the crate re-exports, including zetesis_algebra::{Meter, MeterBytes, PermitLease, Reservation} and zetesis_algebra::words::Words. An exact name locates a declaration; it does not prove the relation sentence or a Rust refinement.

The representations need not have identical names or fields. In particular, Rust Entry relates to Lean Pending, while a concrete Frontier must realize the pending-partition invariant of a Lean walk. The tables state those relations and their remaining obligations explicitly.

Algebra.Subject.cohort_extensive, cohort_monotone and cohort_sound lift existing subjects pointwise to a finite indexed family of regions. Each position retains its own class and subject; cohort_members_iff preserves exactly that position’s class members, and cohort_refuted_iff keeps refutation local to it. cohort_empty leaves the empty family unchanged. These laws specify no batching layout or execution schedule and establish no candidate’s membership. For countermodel queries, different candidates keep their different Countermodels T M classes. The candidate and countercandidate quantifiers, and their reductions, remain those of answer_sets_nested; the atom axis stays inside each region. Concrete cohort rounds, their receipts, and their refinement to these pointwise applications remain implementation obligations.

Intervals, classes and coverage

This relates the concrete interval to Region, not its storage layout.

Values and enumeration verdicts

Rust declaration (kind)Lean declaration (kind)Relation and remaining obligations
zetesis_algebra::reduction::Reduction (trait)Zetesis.AxisFolds.Reduction (structure)The sealed statically dispatched trait supplies pure value operations related to a commutative monoid. Each instance retains its order, bounded-carrier or denotation premises. Value laws neither commute effects nor prove accepted-member coverage.
zetesis_algebra::reduction::All (struct)Zetesis.AxisFolds.all (def)All combines Boolean accepted-member values by conjunction with true as identity and false as absorber; using absorption requires an authenticated nonempty deciding prefix.

Although overflow absorbs mathematically, the runtime never advertises early successful absorption; publishing an exact answer count requires complete distinct-member coverage.

Left representatives on ties, witness retention and optimality proof remain separate from the commutative value law.

Value selection refines denoted minimum when comparison agrees with that order, including distinct Score representations of equal costs. Ordering receipts and retained witnesses are not commutative values.

Iterator exhaustion and finite denotation are required.

For strictly ordered decoded inputs and a comparator faithful to their strict order, ordered_union_sorted_unique proves order and absence of duplicates in the merged stream. The Rust cursor must implement the specified advances, allocation and publication.

Tuple products are the zetesis_algebra::reduction::Reduction implementation for (L, R); there is no separate Rust Product owner. Both coordinates are combined, and both must absorb for the product to absorb. Zetesis.AxisFolds.pair (def), pair_absorbing and pair_idempotent (theorems) state the corresponding laws under the component reductions’ premises. Set-stream functions refine the set values of Zetesis.AxisFolds.inter and Zetesis.AxisFolds.union; they do not implement a fallible Reduction or represent its universal-set identity. An empty stream is not an empty-family verdict. Minimum selection, proof of the optimal cost, exact counting and exhaustion of optimal ties retain distinct contracts.

From the object laws to an execution

Zetesis.Algebra.inside_refl, inside_trans and inside_antisymm describe the region precision order. A Subject is a monotone inflationary map of that poset, or a pointed endofunctor of its thin category; Subject.sound_of_narrower, Subject.apply_sound and Subject.narrow_ideal relate it to the abstraction of its class members under the stated Galois insertion. The common joint closure is an idempotent monad on that thin category, with the closed regions as its algebras; an individual streamed progress step need not be idempotent. The joint_closed, joint_least, joint_extensive, joint_monotone, joint_idempotent, joint_sound and joint_more_subjects theorems, with terminal_agreement, Reaches.eq_joint and fair_iteration_reaches_joint, retain their fixed-family premises. Zetesis.Algebra.refines_wf supplies the finite strict-progress argument.

Rust ranks open atoms only after eager and late agreement. Knowledge must correspond to the intended closure before the same-region/same-split argument applies; the marker trait alone cannot establish that correspondence. zetesis_algebra::walk::inspect classifies a narrowed entry without proving membership or consuming it, and a chosen atom must still be fresh when split. Zetesis.CoverageTree.mem_outputs_iff supplies the accepted-leaf coverage law; Zetesis.Pending.Step.perm and Zetesis.Pending.Walk.exhausted describe pending ownership and exhaustion. A walk unfolds a covering tree; Zetesis.Algebra.Subject.node, LeafVerdict, LeafVerdict.node, answerSetVerdict and countermodelVerdict keep the semantic leaf decision separate from the schedule. An interrupted leaf decision stays undecided. Scalar, parallel, slate and served-query schedules must realize these transitions, including stopped prefixes. Sharing their Rust operations does not itself prove that refinement.

For pure reductions, Zetesis.AxisFolds.Reduction.fold_perm and fold_decided_prefix give value permutation and absorption laws. Complete world-view folding also needs complete accepted-member coverage; repeated members require idempotence or a distinct-member stream as appropriate. Zetesis.Algebra.foldVerdict_absorbed, foldVerdict_complete, foldVerdict_empty, foldVerdict_undecided and foldVerdict_without_absorber keep those outcomes separate. inner_verdict, answer_sets_nested and countermodel_verdict_independent retain the separate answer-set and countermodel quantifiers. No value reduction or verdict carrier supplies the semantic leaf decision, original-input authentication or optimality proof.

The word, meter and permit laws likewise state representation or scalar obligations. They do not prove all concrete layouts, width conversions, allocation failures, polling, synchronization, callback or settlement traces. The correspondence of each consumer and physical implementation remains separate from the existence of its shared Rust operation.

The retained native replay records the earlier zetesis_cpu::cancellation namespace. Its generated Lean, source hashes and replay guards remain tied to that extraction. Qualifying the current zetesis_algebra::cancellation owner requires a new extraction and proof refresh; editing a path or expected hash alone establishes no correspondence.

The reduct query takes the existing authenticated FormulaEvaluation, derives its theory, candidate and frozen truth, and constructs its adapter, subset region and fresh frozen knowledge internally. It accepts no supplied subject or root state. Published query continuations retain their own authenticated entries; they are not new root constructors. Ferraris now indexes its knowledge and private reading context by the sealed class markers. The frozen closure borrows only common worker scratch; its learning capability is unit. A candidate closure can borrow the worker-owned ledger, which is never copied into regional knowledge. The marker does not bind a particular theory, candidate or state; the existing runtime ownership checks remain necessary

What the Rust establishes for those rows, beyond the obligations the arithmetic subjects already carry for forced literals and threshold guards: recognition reads only the masked DAG and the closed root’s knowledge; every probe narrows a copy of the closed query root with exactly the guard and the pattern decided, in the first probing round by the frozen subject and in a later round by the frozen subject composed with the row subjects of the round before, each sound for the class and so their joint closure (Algebra.joint_sound), the complete consistency check of those rows entering as a refuting subject of the class (a 0 = 1 combination under the region’s decisions is a sum of class equations, AlgebraicRows.equation_sum, every variable of which the region decides, equation_excludes_given and excludes_region); so a refuted probe is the premise of entailed_by_refutations with that round’s subject as s. The patterns a clause of the group forbids, and those whose restriction to a group whose support this one contains is such a pattern, are marked refuted without a probe: the region deciding such a pattern lies in the closed root, so a member of the class in it satisfies the clause’s body under the pattern (the clause’s rule and the chains to its base standing in the reduct, their bodies true in the candidate, as the proposal pass reads them) and holds the clause’s guard, which no countermodel in the root holds, cut by the root or a unit by saturation_unit; the region holds no member, nor does its narrowing inside it, which is the same premise, discharged by the proposal pass’s reading of the clause rather than by a probe. A clause too wide for a group whose pattern cuts its whole support is installed as a lower bound of one over that support (AlgebraicRows.lower_of_clause), its all-cut pattern excluded by the same argument. A unit’s probe narrows the closed root, s.narrow (query M), with the guard held, where saturation_unit quantifies over the raw query root with the guard held: a countermodel in the law’s region holds the guard and lies in query M, so by the frozen subject’s soundness it lies in the closed root and, holding the guard, in the probed region, which is how a probe that reaches the candidate or is refuted discharges the law’s premise. A parity row or a count bound is installed only under a guard the closed root cuts, a saturation unit or a residual root’s own decision, and enters without the guard, which the unit discharges (row_under_unit), every region the preparation serves descending from that root; the preparation is built from the theory and the candidate, authenticated at every use, and never consulted for another candidate; add is the only operation changing a parity row; and a stopped probe declines the whole preparation rather than marking a pattern. The affine hull of the allowed patterns and the clique search are trusted computations whose results are checked against the retained pattern tables, not re-read from formulas; the proposal pass’s reading of a clause, where it forbids a pattern without a probe, is a trusted computation beside them.

The support cut (FormulaBounds.unsupported_cut_with_choices) and the objective bound’s own lower-bound reasoning (RequiredChoiceCosts.lower_bound_preserves_answer_sets_strict) still require their full Subject correspondence. StreamedSubjects constructs the elementary subjects of authenticated original constraints and relates completed scans to closure; its concrete cursor refinement remains separate. The approximation-fixpoint reading is a frame, not a claim: regions are its consistent pairs, but downward propagation, learned rows and algebraic rows are not approximators of an immediate-consequence operator, so the joint fixed point is a sound closure relative to a class.

Candidate generation and query representation

Candidate restrictions and storage transformations preserve different objects. A necessary restriction may remove impossible proposals; a query representation must preserve the same classical assignments. Neither operation changes the original program or the reduct used to check membership.

The execution chapter explains these operations in the solver.

The packed Region stores disjoint held and cut masks over real atoms. Knowledge owns one word block with disjoint node-sure, node-never, atom-sure, atom-never, seen and processed chain-witness spans. Its chain-neutral counts (exact until a processed absorbing witness) and exact atom-ranking counts retain their selected width. Splitting the block once into borrowed slices changes no FormulaBounds.Known judgement or propagation charge. Checked span boundaries, complete copying of shape and contents, independent child ownership and truthful retained-byte receipts remain Rust obligations; known_mono does not verify this layout, allocation behavior or performance. Counter widths are chosen from u16, u32 and native width using the largest chain length and initial per-atom parent count. Rust must establish that this bound includes every parent occurrence of every node carrying an atom, including distinct nodes with the same atom. Checked updates, unchanged width during propagation and complete independent copies must preserve those counter meanings. These representation obligations add no premise to the semantic propagation laws. The seen snapshot denotes the region decisions already incorporated; differencing the current decided mask supplies only new decisions, and the completed snapshot also includes atoms learned by propagation. FormulaBounds.known_mono supplies the mathematical ancestor-inheritance law. The Rust API additionally requires the same narrower, theory, producer set and frozen truth, and knowledge closed for an enclosing region. The law neither proves the packed representation nor validates those unchecked caller preconditions. Exact word/index conversion, zero unused tail bits, polarity decoding, complete seen snapshots and correct child cloning remain Rust obligations. The cross-word original/frozen regressions are executable evidence for those boundaries, not formal refinement. Retained-byte accounting includes the owned masks; the full seen-mask scan and snapshot writes are outside the existing charged-read work counters.

The producer support continuation retains two positions in each long head row. Every producer before the first and strictly between the two positions has been proved blocked by a false body or a competing held ordinary head. Those facts are monotone within descendants under the same original subject. Both remaining endpoints are rechecked; only complete coverage can establish no support or sole support. An open head’s first witness cannot substitute for the second witness required after that head becomes held. Choices keep their existing support rule. known_blocked_mono and known_choice_blocked_mono transfer the existing ordinary and atomic-choice blocking judgments to every region inside the first, using known_mono. These laws preserve blocked witnesses, not the number of unblocked witnesses: a sole remaining supporter may later become blocked too. known_blocked_no_support, known_choice_blocked_no_support, unsupported_cut_with_choices and the sole-support laws establish their semantic consequences. They do not verify the Rust cursor or define a complete support Subject. Exact row identities and bounds, complete prefix coverage, independent cloning and parent restoration, metered initialization, typed interruption and actual-capacity receipts remain executable representation obligations. No continuation state is used for frozen-reduct or candidate-only restriction narrowing.

The chain accumulator retains exactly the information its consumers read. For disjunction, false operands are neutral and a true operand is absorbing; for conjunction these roles are reversed. ChainEvidence.records_counts and propagation_observations show that one neutral count and an absorbing witness preserve the observations of two exact counts after every finite sequence of processed notifications. The witness is set when an operand event is processed, not when its node bit first changes. Rust must establish that each relevant operand occurrence supplies exactly its applicable notification, that frozen masks skip the same events, and that parent decisions, queues and charged work are unchanged. The abstract accumulator laws do not establish those event-loop or packed-word properties. ChainEvidence.settled_record_observations and settled_records_observations additionally show that ignoring notifications after a processed absorbing witness preserves the observations relevant to an unrefuted chain. The Rust parent dispatcher applies this rule only after the same event has established the root at its absorbing polarity. Its neutral count is then retained unchanged; pending node bits do not establish that witness. The parent visit remains charged, and every node event, other parent, support wake-up and split-ranking update remains active. The laws do not establish that Rust reaches only these consistent states or preserves those other obligations.

The last-operand scan in Closure::unit can return unchanged when an already processed operand witnesses the required polarity: sure for a disjunction, never for a conjunction. Its callers have counted every other operand at the opposite polarity, so the sole target is already known. The existing FormulaChains.disj_chain_unit and conj_chain_unit laws supply the semantic unit rule, not this counter implementation. Rust must establish unique operand incidences, counts that never lead their corresponding bits, preserved pending events and contradiction handling. A set bit whose event is still pending does not alone justify the shortcut. The omitted scan changes charged work and resource-limited prefixes; no exact old work count is claimed.

The same processed-count invariant permits Closure::teach_chain to omit a complete downward scan when every conjunction operand is already sure, or every disjunction operand is already never. Each omitted update would be unchanged. The root event still updates parents, ranking and support wakeups. Pending bits without a complete processed count retain the scan. This does not change the FormulaChains laws or discharge the concrete queue and counter obligations.

A propagation operation stops when it first establishes contradiction. The remaining operands, parents and support wakeups cannot restore a model: FormulaBounds.known_contradiction_refutes excludes every answer set in that region. Rust must abandon its unfinished knowledge, restore borrowed state and clear pending scratch before reuse. The earlier exit charges only work actually visited; it may establish refutation before a quota would have stopped the old trailing scan. This is a semantic justification, not a proof of those Rust state-management obligations.

The region candidate walk and frozen proper-subset queries share one immutable index constructed with the exact original Theory, built by its one owner when the walk first needs it. Reuse checks instance identity. Each region or query retains private Knowledge, and each candidate supplies freshly authenticated frozen truth. Sharing preserves the subjects of the existing FormulaBounds and ReductRegions laws, and building the index later builds the same index; it changes ownership and timing, not the definition of a reduct. Index construction, identity checks, mutable-state separation and attribution of construction work remain Rust refinement obligations.

The immutable region adjacency stores each ordered incidence row as a slice between two offsets in one contiguous entry vector. AdjacencyRows proves exact slices from concatenated mathematical rows and unchanged ordered row folds. Decoding every Rust row must recover that original occurrence list exactly, including duplicate atom occurrences and original producer identity; equality of membership sets alone would not preserve chain counters, split ranking or bounded traversal prefixes. The same node used on both sides of an implication is still coalesced by the existing incidence construction, before storage compaction. Distinct atom nodes carrying the same atom remain distinct incidences. Exact row decoding leaves the FormulaBounds, FormulaChains and frozen ReductRegions rules unchanged. Those semantic laws do not establish the Rust count/prefix/scatter construction, machine offsets, reservation failures or event order. Ordered-row and existing propagation regressions provide executable evidence for those correspondences. The checked compact builder adds linear construction passes while retaining the existing logical node-index receipt; it does not change mutable Knowledge or its copy behavior, and does not claim that all index allocations are fallible.

Chain preparation classifies single-parent interiors before collecting each maximal chain once. It preserves root identity, left-to-right distinct operands and the boundary at shared or asserted nodes. The existing FormulaChains laws therefore remain the semantic contract. Differential tests compare the concrete collector with a bounded recursive definition; these are implementation evidence, not an extracted Lean proof of the collector. Current Rust formula storage retains native conjunction and disjunction rows: pairs are inline, wider rows use the paired operand arena, and NodeView exposes every operand. The abstract OperandArena and OperandTable laws specify row decoding and original/frozen truth. The extracted NativeRows and NativeRowsArena laws check the row getters and their ordered-list bridge. NativeAdmittedData and NativeExecution add actual paired-table admission and completed original/frozen evaluation. Public membership, runtime effects and source-compiler correspondence remain separate obligations.

The batched parallel proposer separates classical candidate production from membership. Its workers use the original region readings and disjoint splits; they do not certify stable models. Read Frontier with a proposal family that contains every still-required stable interpretation. Necessary support cuts may exclude other classical models, so classical truth alone is not the proposal coverage predicate. FormulaBounds supplies the preservation premises for these cuts and decided classical leaves. Pending.Walk.perm accounts for leaves emitted so far together with those still held by the frontier. The producers’ frontier is their deques together with the region each producer holds: a split publishes one child and keeps the other in hand, a steal or a return to a deque only transfers ownership, and the count of unresolved regions is raised before a published child becomes visible. A leaf that finds every output slot reserved returns its region to a deque unresolved, which again only transfers ownership, and a return refused entry capacity records a stop. So every stop-free step permutes that frontier and the emitted leaves, and a slate reports exhaustion only from a stop-free join at a count of zero. The count, the hands that bound the regions in hand, the output-slot reservation at a leaf that bounds the emitted candidates, the stop a refused return records, and the hand-over are Rust obligations beside the walker’s queue and gate protocols, as is the stop’s order: a failed region returns to a deque only after the stop closes the slate, and a producer checks for the close after each take, so no region is stepped again after its step failed. An optimizing search’s producers share one deque, taking the region published most recently; the frontier is still the deques and the regions in hand, every transition only moves a region between them, and the same permutation argument applies. Only the order of exploration, and the bound on queued regions, differ.

After producers join, emitted candidates enter the pending membership ledger. BatchAccounting.exact_commit_preserves_soundness justifies committing a fully classified prefix; completed_results_exact additionally requires coverage and an empty queued and pending remainder without delayed failure. Batch capacity is a scheduling boundary, not exhaustion. A producer stop retains completed candidates and reports the unresolved remainder as incomplete; it cannot turn an empty delivered batch into a complete negative result. The concrete queue ownership, reservation arithmetic, panic/cancellation paths, budget settlement before checking and transfer between slates remain Rust obligations. The two abstract laws do not themselves verify that concurrent implementation.

Joined producers retain source checkers and narrowing scratch across slates. A stable owner outlives every borrowed checker; a producer’s workspace is used by one task at a time and keeps no candidate knowledge. Candidate knowledge remains with the frontier entry. Terminal cleanup releases the workspaces without changing pending candidates or failure receipts. These ownership and reuse invariants, including the owner/dependent container, remain Rust correspondence obligations; they introduce no new answer-set law and are not established by the existing batch theorems.

The CPU batched completion and the GPU formula routes share one internal batch boundary. Independent routes check original satisfaction before invoking a checker; joint routes establish it together with the reduct verdict.
